CODE
Art. 2.3.68. 
Composition of the final patrimony
The final patrimony consists of the property belonging to the spouse on the date of the dissolution of the regime. Debts are taken into account, even when they exceed the amount of the assets.  
It is added to the final patrimony the value of property which a spouse: 
1¡ has donated, except: 
a) if the donation is not excessive having regard to the lifestyle of the spouses or; 
b) if the donation relates to property of the original estate donated to relatives in the direct line. However, the increase in value brought about by improvements made to this property, during the duration of the matrimonial property regime, with a sum of money that does not depend on the original patrimony, is added to the final patrimony; 
2¡ has been sold with the aim of injuring the other spouse or; 
3¡ has been dissipated.
These provisions do not apply if the gift, fraudulent alienation or dissipation occurred more than ten years before the dissolution of the matrimonial regime or if the other spouse consented thereto.
